qs.p: The glacier's retreat has been ______ rather than steady: years of rapid melting have alternated with long periods in which the ice front barely moved.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
qs.e: Retreat that alternates between rapid melting and near-standstill occurs in bursts: it is "intermittent." "Uniform" means steady, which the text rejects. "Imperceptible" contradicts "years of rapid melting," and "inexorable" (impossible to stop) says nothing about the stop-and-start pattern.

qs.p: Many readers find the essayist's arguments ______, since she supports nearly every claim with carefully documented evidence and anticipates the most serious objections.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
qs.e: Arguments backed by documented evidence and that address objections are clear and convincing: "cogent." "Specious" (plausible but false) is the opposite. "Digressive" (wandering off topic) and "sentimental" (overly emotional) aren't supported by the description.

qs.p: The playwright's dialogue captures the ______ of everyday conversation: characters interrupt one another, trail off in the middle of sentences, and repeat themselves, just as real people do.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
qs.e: Interruptions, unfinished sentences, and repetition describe the disorderly quality of real talk: its "messiness." "Formality," "eloquence," and "precision" all describe polished speech, the opposite of what the examples show.

qs.p: The following text is adapted from a novel.The doctor delivered the news with the air of a man reporting tomorrow's weather, and it was only on the walk home that Mira began to understand what he had told her.
qs.q: As used in the text, what does the word "air" most nearly mean?
qs.e: The doctor spoke as casually as someone giving a weather report; "air" here means his manner or bearing. "Atmosphere" and "breeze" refer to the air around us, and "melody" is the musical sense of "air." None describes how a person behaves.

qs.p: Unlike its ______ predecessor, which filled an entire room and required a team of technicians to operate, the new computer fit on a single desk.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
qs.e: A machine that filled a room and needed a team to run it was bulky and awkward: "cumbersome." "Portable" contradicts the room-sized description, and "affordable" and "reliable" don't relate to size or the contrast with a desk-sized computer.

qs.p: In the nineteenth century, most public libraries kept their books in closed stacks: patrons requested a title at a desk, and a clerk retrieved it. When libraries began opening their shelves to the public around 1900, some librarians worried that books would be stolen or misplaced. Advocates of open shelves countered that letting patrons browse would lead them to discover books they would never have thought to request.
qs.q: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
c: To describe a change in library practice and the arguments for and against it
To argue that closed stacks protected books better than open shelves
To show that open shelves led to a sharp increase in stolen books
To explain how clerks organized books in nineteenth-century libraries
qs.e: The text describes a shift from closed stacks to open shelves and presents both the worry about theft and the advocates' argument for browsing. It takes no side, doesn't explain how books were organized, and reports a fear of theft rather than evidence that theft increased.

qs.p: Gardeners often welcome earthworms, which loosen and enrich soil. <u>In the northern hardwood forests of North America, however, there were no native earthworms after the glaciers of the last ice age retreated.</u> Worms introduced by European settlers, often in soil and the roots of imported plants, now consume the thick layer of fallen leaves on which many native wildflowers and salamanders depend.
qs.q: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
c: It describes the benefits that earthworms provide to gardens.
It explains how earthworms were transported to North America.
It provides background explaining why earthworms in these forests are an introduced species with harmful effects.
It presents evidence that earthworms survived the last ice age.
qs.e: The underlined sentence establishes that these forests had no native earthworms, which is why the worms there are introduced and why their effects, described next, are harmful. The garden benefits come before it, transport is described in the next sentence, and the sentence says worms did not survive in these forests after the ice age.

qs.p: Text 1Some historians of science portray the Scientific Revolution of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries as a sudden break with medieval thought, in which thinkers such as Galileo replaced centuries of speculation with mathematics and experiment.Text 2Historian Thomas Elwood points out that many ideas credited to that period had medieval roots. In the fourteenth century, scholars at Oxford and Paris had already developed mathematical descriptions of motion, including the "mean speed theorem," which Galileo later used in his study of falling bodies.
qs.q: Based on the texts, how would Elwood (Text 2) most likely respond to the portrayal in Text 1?
c: He would agree that medieval scholars made no use of mathematics.
He would argue that Galileo did not study falling bodies.
He would claim that the Scientific Revolution took place in the fourteenth century.
He would argue that it underestimates how much the period built on earlier medieval work.
qs.e: Text 1 describes a "sudden break"; Elwood shows that a key mathematical idea Galileo used came from fourteenth-century scholars, which points to continuity. He shows medieval scholars did use mathematics, says Galileo studied falling bodies, and doesn't relocate the Scientific Revolution to the fourteenth century.

qs.p: The following text is adapted from a short story.When Kiri's younger brother asked her to read his first short story, she promised to be honest. She read it twice at the kitchen table, underlining sentences and filling the margins with questions. But when he came to collect it, she looked at his face, then at the pages crowded with her handwriting, and said only that she had liked the ending. She would give him the notes, she decided, after his next story.
qs.q: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
c: Kiri decides to hold back her detailed criticism for now in order to spare her brother's feelings.
Kiri dislikes her brother's story and tells him so directly.
Kiri's brother refuses to accept any criticism of his story.
Kiri forgets to give her brother the notes she wrote.
qs.e: Kiri prepared extensive notes, but after seeing her brother's face she offers only praise and decides to give the notes later, a deliberate choice to protect his feelings. She doesn't criticize him directly, she remembers the notes (she chooses to delay them), and the text says nothing about how he would react to criticism.

qs.p: Sea otters are among the few marine mammals that use tools. Floating on their backs, they balance a rock on their chests and crack open clams and sea urchins against it. Some otters keep a favorite rock for repeated use, tucking it into a loose pouch of skin under each forearm, where they also store food gathered during a dive.
qs.q: According to the text, how do some sea otters carry a rock for repeated use?
c: By tucking it into a loose pouch of skin under a forearm
By leaving it on the shore and returning to it after each dive
By holding it in their mouths during dives
By balancing it on their chests while they swim underwater
qs.e: The last sentence says some otters tuck a favorite rock into a pouch of skin under the forearm. The chest is where they balance the rock while eating at the surface, and the text doesn't mention carrying rocks in their mouths or leaving them on shore.

qs.p: Many songbirds sing most intensely around dawn. One explanation, the acoustic transmission hypothesis, holds that birds sing then because the cool, still air of early morning carries sound farther than the warmer, more turbulent air later in the day.
qs.q: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the acoustic transmission hypothesis?
c: Some songbird species also sing intensely around dusk.
Birds that sing at dawn are more likely to find food later in the morning.
Recordings of birdsong played at dawn could be detected at greater distances than the same recordings played at midday.
Songbirds sing less on rainy mornings than on clear mornings.
qs.e: The hypothesis claims that dawn air carries sound farther. Showing that identical recordings travel farther at dawn than at midday tests exactly that. Feeding success, rainy-day singing, and dusk singing don't directly show anything about how far sound travels at dawn.

qs.p: In Walt Whitman's 1865 poem "When I Heard the Learn'd Astronomer," the speaker attends a lecture on astronomy but finds direct experience of the night sky more meaningful than the lecture's charts and calculations.
qs.q: Which quotation from the poem most effectively illustrates the claim?
c: "How soon unaccountable I became tired and sick,"
"When the proofs, the figures, were ranged in columns before me,"
"Till rising and gliding out I wander'd off by myself, / In the mystical moist night-air, and from time to time, / Look'd up in perfect silence at the stars."
qs.e: The claim contrasts the lecture with direct experience. Choice D shows the speaker leaving the lecture to look at the stars in silence, choosing direct experience. Choices A and C describe only the lecture, and choice B shows dissatisfaction without what the speaker turns to instead.

qs.p:
Applications and Admissions to Four Graduate Programs
ProgramApplicantsAdmitted
A400100
B25075
C900135
D15030
A university administrator notes that although Program C received by far the most applications, it was also the most selective of the four programs, admitting the smallest share of its applicants.
qs.q: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the administrator's statement?
c: Program D received the fewest applications of the four programs.
Program C admitted 135 of its 900 applicants, or 15 percent, a smaller share than any other program admitted.
Program B admitted 30 percent of its applicants, the largest share of any program.
Program C admitted more applicants than any of the other programs did.
qs.e: Selectivity is the share admitted. The rates are A 25%, B 30%, C 15%, D 20%, so C's 15% is the lowest. Choice D is true but describes a count, not a share (and, if anything, might suggest the opposite). Choices A and C describe other programs without showing that C admitted the smallest share.

qs.p: As lava cools, grains of the mineral magnetite within it align with Earth's magnetic field, and the rock preserves that alignment after it hardens. Studies of rocks of many ages show that Earth's magnetic field has reversed direction many times, with north and south switching places. Two lava flows whose magnetite points in opposite directions therefore ______
qs.q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
c: most likely formed at different times, separated by at least one reversal of the magnetic field.
must have cooled at exactly the same moment.
could not have formed on Earth.
qs.e: Rock records the field's direction at the time it cooled. Opposite orientations mean the field pointed in different directions when each flow cooled, so they formed at different times with a reversal in between. Simultaneous cooling would give the same orientation, and both flows contain magnetite.

qs.p: When a city introduced a fee for driving into its downtown during weekday business hours, car traffic in the area fell by about 20 percent. Downtown retailers had warned that the fee would reduce their sales, but over the following year, shop revenues in the area remained stable. One possible explanation for this outcome is that ______
qs.q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
c: downtown shops closed during the hours when the fee applied.
many downtown shoppers had already been arriving by public transit, on foot, or by bicycle rather than by car.
the fee caused car traffic downtown to increase.
shoppers who drove downtown spent less money than they had before.
qs.e: If many shoppers weren't driving in the first place, a fee on driving would barely affect them, so sales could stay stable even as car traffic fell. Shops closing during fee hours would hurt revenue, the text says traffic fell, and drivers spending less would push revenue down, not explain why it held steady.

qs.p: Coral reefs cover less than 1 percent of the ocean ______ they support roughly a quarter of all known marine species.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
qs.e: Two independent clauses must be separated by a semicolon (or period); "nevertheless" is a conjunctive adverb that begins the second clause and is followed by a comma. Commas alone create a comma splice, no punctuation creates a run-on, and omitting the comma after "nevertheless" is incorrect.

qs.p: Among the most serious problems facing early aviators ______ the tendency of their aircraft to stall at low speeds.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
qs.e: In this inverted sentence, the subject follows the verb: "the tendency … to stall at low speeds." "Tendency" is singular, so the verb is "was." "Problems" and "aviators" belong to the introductory phrase and don't control the verb.

qs.p: Marie and Pierre Curie shared ______ 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with Henri Becquerel for research on radioactivity.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
qs.e: The prize belonged to both Marie and Pierre, a plural antecedent, so the plural possessive "their" is correct. "Its" is singular and refers to things, "her" refers only to Marie, and "they're" means "they are."

qs.p: ______ the entire manuscript twice, the editor returned it to the author with only a few minor suggestions.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
qs.e: The opening phrase describes an action the editor completed before returning the manuscript, so "Having read" (a perfect participle) is correct. "Had read" and "has read" are finite verbs that would create a sentence without a proper connection, and "To have read" doesn't describe the editor's completed action.

qs.p: In ______ the year the first transatlantic telegraph cable was completed, Queen Victoria and President James Buchanan exchanged messages across the Atlantic Ocean.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
qs.e: "The year the first transatlantic telegraph cable was completed" renames 1858 and is set off by commas; the closing comma after "completed" requires an opening comma after "1858." A semicolon or colon would break the introductory phrase from the main clause.

qs.p: Midway through the novel, the narrator returns to her childhood home and ______ that the orchard her grandfather planted has been cut down.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
qs.e: The sentence describes the novel's events in the present tense ("returns"), and the second verb in the pair must match: "discovers." Switching to the past or future breaks the consistent tense.

qs.p: Penguins cannot fly. ______ their wings, which have evolved into stiff, narrow flippers, make them remarkably fast and agile swimmers.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
qs.e: Penguins' wings serve a different purpose (swimming) in place of flying, so "Instead" fits. "Similarly" and "For example" don't express a replacement, and "As a result" wrongly suggests that their inability to fly causes the flippers.

qs.p: Many early photographic processes required subjects to remain perfectly still for several minutes. ______ portraits from the 1840s often show sitters with stiff postures and unsmiling expressions.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
qs.e: Holding still for minutes explains the stiff, unsmiling portraits, so the second sentence is a result of the first: "Consequently." "Nonetheless" and "By contrast" signal opposition, and "Likewise" signals similarity.

qs.p: Voters rejected the council's first proposal, which would have raised the local sales tax by one percentage point. Its revised proposal, ______ passed easily after the increase was cut in half.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
qs.e: The revised proposal's easy passage contrasts with the first proposal's rejection, so "on the other hand" fits. "In other words" signals restatement, "likewise" signals similarity, and "as a result" would claim the passage was caused by the rejection itself.

qs.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Mount Everest lies on the border between China and Nepal.
  • Its height has been measured many times since the 1800s, with slightly different results.
  • In 2020, China and Nepal jointly announced a new official height.
  • The announced height was 8,848.86 meters.
qs.q: The student wants to describe the most recent official measurement of Mount Everest. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
c: Measurements of Mount Everest have produced slightly different results over the years.
The height of Mount Everest has been measured many times since the 1800s.
In 2020, China and Nepal jointly announced a new official height for Mount Everest: 8,848.86 meters.
Mount Everest lies on the border between China and Nepal.
qs.e: Only choice C describes the 2020 measurement, giving who announced it and the height. The others give location or general history without describing the latest measurement.

qs.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Desalination removes salt from seawater to produce fresh water.
  • Thermal distillation boils seawater and condenses the vapor.
  • Reverse osmosis pushes seawater through membranes that block salt.
  • Reverse osmosis typically uses less energy than thermal distillation.
  • Reverse osmosis now produces most of the world's desalinated water.
qs.q: The student wants to suggest a reason that reverse osmosis has become the dominant desalination method. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
c: Reverse osmosis pushes seawater through membranes that block salt.
Reverse osmosis, which typically uses less energy than thermal distillation, now produces most of the world's desalinated water.
Desalination removes salt from seawater to produce fresh water.
Thermal distillation boils seawater and condenses the vapor to produce fresh water.
qs.e: Choice B pairs reverse osmosis's dominance with a plausible reason (lower energy use). The others describe how a method works or what desalination is, without suggesting why reverse osmosis prevails.

qs.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Wangari Maathai was a Kenyan environmental activist.
  • In 1977 she founded the Green Belt Movement.
  • The movement organized women to plant tens of millions of trees.
  • In 2004, Maathai became the first African woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.
qs.q: The student wants to emphasize the historic nature of Maathai's 2004 achievement. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
c: Wangari Maathai founded the Green Belt Movement in 1977.
The Green Belt Movement organized women to plant tens of millions of trees.
In 2004, Kenyan activist Wangari Maathai became the first African woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.
Wangari Maathai was a Kenyan environmental activist who received the Nobel Peace Prize.
qs.e: What made the achievement historic was that she was the first African woman to win the prize. Only choice C states that. Choice D mentions the prize but leaves out the "first," and the others concern the Green Belt Movement.

qs.p: The agency's response to the residents' complaint was ______: it acknowledged receiving their letter but addressed none of the specific concerns raised in it.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
qs.e: A reply that only acknowledges receipt without engaging any concern is done as a mere formality: "perfunctory." "Exhaustive" is the opposite. "Conciliatory" (seeking to placate) and "scathing" (harshly critical) both imply real engagement with the complaint.

qs.p: The scholar's interpretation is ______ at best: it rests entirely on a single ambiguous phrase in a letter whose authenticity is itself disputed.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
qs.e: An interpretation resting on one ambiguous phrase in a possibly inauthentic letter has very weak support: it is "tenuous." "Incontestable" is the opposite. "Pedantic" (overly concerned with minor details) and "sweeping" (broad) don't describe weak support.

qs.p: The frog's range has ______ dramatically as its forest habitat has been cleared; once found across three countries, the species now survives only in a handful of isolated valleys.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
qs.e: Going from three countries to a few valleys means the range has shrunk: "contracted." "Diversified" and "fluctuated" don't describe steady shrinking, and "migrated" means moved, not reduced.

qs.p: The following text is adapted from an essay on poetry.Poets have always claimed a certain license with grammar, bending a sentence until it nearly breaks so that a single word lands with the force they intend.
qs.q: As used in the text, what does the word "license" most nearly mean?
qs.e: "Poetic license" is the freedom to depart from ordinary rules, as described by bending sentences until they nearly break. "Permit" refers to an official document, "approval" to someone else's consent, and "authority" to the power to command, none of which fits.

qs.p: Although the theory was greeted with skepticism when it was first proposed, later experiments have ______ its central predictions, and it is now widely accepted.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
qs.e: The theory became widely accepted after experiments, so those experiments must have confirmed its predictions: "borne out." "Called into question" would undermine acceptance, "overlooked" means ignored, and experiments can't "anticipate" predictions made before them.

qs.p: The English word "decimate" comes from a Roman military punishment in which one soldier in ten was killed. Some critics insist that the word should therefore be used only to mean "destroy one-tenth of something." Linguist Ana Ferreira argues, however, that a word's meaning is determined by how speakers actually use it, and by that standard "decimate" now means "destroy a large part of," whatever its origin.
qs.q: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
c: To argue that "decimate" should be used only in its original sense
To present a linguist's view about how a word's meaning should be determined
To explain how the Roman army punished its soldiers
To list words whose meanings have changed since Roman times
qs.e: The text sets up a dispute over "decimate" and presents Ferreira's position that usage, not origin, determines meaning. The Roman punishment is background, choice A is the critics' view that Ferreira rejects, and only one word is discussed.

qs.p: Glaciologists once assumed that the base of the Antarctic ice sheet was frozen solid to the bedrock beneath it. <u>Radar surveys beginning in the 1960s, however, revealed hundreds of lakes of liquid water trapped beneath the ice, kept from freezing by the pressure of the ice above and by heat rising from Earth's interior.</u> The largest, Lake Vostok, lies under nearly four kilometers of ice. These discoveries have raised the possibility that microbial life could survive in such isolated environments.
qs.q: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
c: It describes the methods glaciologists used to measure the thickness of the ice sheet.
It explains why microbial life could not survive beneath the Antarctic ice.
It presents a discovery that overturned an earlier assumption and that the rest of the text builds on.
It provides an example that supports the assumption described in the first sentence.
qs.e: The underlined sentence, signaled by "however," reports radar evidence of liquid lakes, contradicting the assumption that the base was frozen. The next sentences develop it (Lake Vostok, possible life). It mentions radar only as a source of the discovery, says nothing against microbial life, and contradicts rather than supports the first sentence.

qs.p: Text 1Many archaeologists have argued that the islanders of Rapa Nui (Easter Island) moved their giant stone statues, the moai, by dragging them horizontally on wooden sledges, a method requiring many workers and large amounts of timber. The deforestation that resulted, they argue, contributed to the decline of the island's society.Text 2Archaeologists Terry Hunt and Carl Lipo propose that the moai were instead "walked" upright: teams pulling ropes from alternating sides rocked each statue forward. In a 2012 experiment, a team of eighteen people used this method to move a replica moai weighing about 4.4 metric tons a distance of roughly 100 meters, using no wooden sledges.
qs.q: Based on the texts, how would Hunt and Lipo (Text 2) most likely respond to the argument in Text 1 about deforestation?
c: They would agree that dragging the moai on sledges caused the island's deforestation.
They would argue that the moai were never moved from where they were carved.
They would argue that moving the moai may not have required the large amounts of timber that the argument assumes.
They would claim that eighteen people could not have moved a statue weighing several tons.
qs.e: The deforestation argument depends on moving the moai having used lots of timber. Hunt and Lipo's method uses ropes and few people and no sledges, which undercuts that assumption. They propose a different method rather than agreeing with sledges, they agree the statues were moved, and their experiment showed eighteen people could move one.

qs.p: When European explorers encountered the stone ruins of Great Zimbabwe in the late nineteenth century, many insisted that the city must have been built by foreigners. Excavations in the twentieth century, however, showed that it was constructed between the eleventh and fifteenth centuries by ancestors of the Shona people, who still live in the region. Historians now regard the explorers' claims as having reflected their own prejudices rather than any evidence at the site.
qs.q: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
c: Archaeological evidence showed that Great Zimbabwe was built by ancestors of local people, discrediting earlier claims rooted in prejudice.
Historians continue to debate who built Great Zimbabwe.
European explorers were the first people to study the ruins of Great Zimbabwe scientifically.
Great Zimbabwe was abandoned by the Shona people in the nineteenth century.
qs.e: The text contrasts explorers' claims with excavation findings and concludes that the claims reflected prejudice. The explorers' claims are described as unscientific, the text gives construction dates (eleventh to fifteenth centuries), not an abandonment date, and it presents a settled conclusion, not an ongoing debate.

qs.p: The following text is adapted from a novel.Mr. Tanaka had stopped winding the clock in the hall after his wife died. It was she who had kept it, every Sunday after breakfast, and he could not bring himself to take over the small ritual. Visitors assumed the clock was broken. He let them think so.
qs.q: Based on the text, why has Mr. Tanaka stopped winding the clock?
c: The clock is broken and cannot be repaired.
Winding it was a ritual associated with his late wife that he cannot bear to continue.
He wants visitors to believe that he has no interest in clocks.
He never knew how to wind the clock.
qs.e: The text says his wife wound it every Sunday and that "he could not bring himself to take over the small ritual," showing that grief keeps him from doing it. Visitors only assume the clock is broken; nothing says he doesn't know how to wind it, and letting visitors believe it is broken hides his grief rather than expressing disinterest.

qs.p: In 2015, a city opened a bus rapid transit line with dedicated lanes and frequent service. Economist Sven Lund claims that the new line caused property values to rise in neighborhoods near its stations.
qs.q: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Lund's claim?
c: Ridership on the new line exceeded the city's projections in its first year.
Property values near the stations rose more than the citywide average.
Property values rose by the same amount in neighborhoods with similar characteristics that were far from any station.
Several new businesses opened near the line's stations after 2015.
qs.e: If comparable neighborhoods far from the line saw the same increase, something other than the line likely drove the rise, which undercuts the causal claim. High ridership and new businesses are consistent with the line's influence, and above-average growth near stations would support the claim.

qs.p: In a study of sleep and attention, researchers measured average reaction times on a simple task and a complex task for three groups: rested participants, sleep-deprived participants, and sleep-deprived participants who had been given caffeine. The researchers concluded that caffeine largely offset the effects of sleep deprivation on the simple task but not on the complex task.
qs.q: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the researchers' conclusion?
c: On both tasks, sleep-deprived participants without caffeine had the slowest reaction times.

On the simple task, sleep-deprived participants given caffeine responded nearly as quickly as rested participants, but on the complex task they responded nearly as slowly as sleep-deprived participants without caffeine.
All three groups had slower reaction times on the complex task than on the simple task.
On the complex task, rested participants had an average reaction time of about 450 milliseconds.
qs.e: The conclusion contrasts caffeine's effect on the two tasks. Choice B shows both halves: on the simple task the caffeine group (about 260 ms) is close to the rested group (about 250 ms), while on the complex task it (about 630 ms) is close to the sleep-deprived group (about 650 ms). The other choices are accurate but don't compare caffeine's effect across tasks.

qs.p: In Sara Teasdale's 1918 poem "There Will Come Soft Rains," the speaker imagines a world after a devastating war and suggests that nature would not notice or mourn even the complete extinction of humankind.
qs.q: Which quotation from the poem most effectively illustrates the claim?
c: "Not one would mind, neither bird nor tree, / If mankind perished utterly;"
"And swallows circling with their shimmering sound;"
"There will come soft rains and the smell of the ground,"
"Robins will wear their feathery fire / Whistling their whims on a low fence-wire;"
qs.e: The claim is that nature would be indifferent to humanity's complete disappearance. Choice A says that no bird or tree would mind "if mankind perished utterly." The other quotations describe nature continuing peacefully but don't address its indifference to human extinction.

qs.p: After a larger predatory fish was introduced to a lake, the population of a small fish that it preys on declined. Ecologists expected the zooplankton eaten by the small fish to increase as a result, but the zooplankton population declined instead. Further study revealed that young individuals of the predatory species eat large quantities of zooplankton before they grow large enough to hunt fish. This finding suggests that ______
qs.q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
c: the zooplankton declined because the small fish began eating more of them.
the small fish population increased after the predator was introduced.
the zooplankton decline may have resulted from direct feeding by young predators, outweighing the benefit to zooplankton of having fewer small fish.
adult predatory fish eat more zooplankton than young predatory fish do.
qs.e: Fewer small fish should have meant more zooplankton, but the newly introduced predator's young also eat zooplankton, which can explain the unexpected decline. The text says the small fish declined; fewer small fish couldn't eat more zooplankton; and the text says young predators, not adults, eat zooplankton.

qs.p: Researchers asked beachgoers to estimate their chance of being bitten by a shark in a given year. Nearly all estimates were far higher than the actual risk, and the overestimates were largest among people who reported having recently seen news stories about shark attacks. One possible explanation for these results is that ______
qs.q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
c: vivid reports of rare events may lead people to judge those events to be more common than they actually are.
people who swim more often are more likely to be bitten by sharks.
beachgoers who had not seen such stories underestimated the risk of being bitten.
news stories about shark attacks usually exaggerate the number of attacks that occur.
qs.e: Recent exposure to dramatic stories was linked to bigger overestimates, which suggests that memorable reports make rare events seem more frequent. Nothing in the study concerns swimming frequency or exaggerated reporting, and the text says nearly all participants overestimated.

qs.p: The seventeenth-century official Samuel Pepys wrote his famous diary in ______ a system of abbreviated symbols that kept its contents hidden from casual readers.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
qs.e: "A system of abbreviated symbols…" is an appositive renaming "shorthand," so it is set off with a comma. Without punctuation the phrase runs into "shorthand," a semicolon requires an independent clause after it, and "which" leaves the clause without a verb.

qs.p: A pair of ivory-billed woodpeckers, a species last confirmed in the region decades ago, ______ reportedly been seen nesting in the reserve.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
qs.e: The subject is "A pair," which is singular, so the singular verb "has" is required. "Woodpeckers" is part of the phrase "of ivory-billed woodpeckers" and doesn't control the verb.

qs.p: ______ Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera drew heavily on pre-Columbian art in their work.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
qs.e: "Such as Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera" identifies which painters are meant, so it is essential and takes no commas. A single comma before "such as" would open a nonessential phrase that is never closed, a comma after "such as" separates it from its examples, and a semicolon breaks the sentence.

qs.p: By the time the rescue team reached the stranded climbers, the storm ______ for nearly six hours.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
qs.e: The storm's raging continued up to a past moment (when the team reached the climbers), which calls for the past perfect progressive: "had been raging." The other forms point to the present or future.

qs.p: The question that guided the study ______ the city's new bike lanes had reduced traffic injuries.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
qs.e: "Whether the city's new bike lanes had reduced traffic injuries" is the complement of the verb "was," and no punctuation belongs between a verb and its complement. A colon requires a complete clause before it, and a comma or semicolon would also wrongly split the verb from its complement.

qs.p: The silver coins that archaeologists found buried in the farmer's field, along with a single bronze ring, ______ to the reign of the Roman emperor Hadrian.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
qs.e: The subject is "coins," which is plural. "Along with a single bronze ring" is an added phrase that doesn't change the subject's number, and "field" is inside the relative clause. A plural subject takes "date."

qs.p: Some critics have described the architect's concrete buildings as cold and forbidding. Her admirers, ______ praise the same buildings for their calm, unadorned clarity.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
qs.e: The admirers' praise is a contrasting view held alongside the critics' complaint. "Meanwhile" presents that parallel, opposing perspective. "Therefore" implies a consequence, "for instance" an example of the critics' view, and "similarly" agreement.

qs.p: Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine against smallpox in 1796. ______ it took nearly two centuries of vaccination campaigns before the World Health Organization declared the disease eradicated in 1980.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
qs.e: One might expect a vaccine to end a disease quickly, yet eradication took nearly two centuries. "Even so" signals that something occurred despite what came before. "Thus" implies the long delay was a consequence of the vaccine's development, and "For example" and "Similarly" don't fit.

qs.p: In laboratory tests, the new coating prevented ice from forming on model aircraft wings at temperatures as low as −20°C. ______ trials on actual aircraft are still needed to determine whether the coating performs as well under real flight conditions.
qs.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
qs.e: Despite promising lab results, more testing is required: the second sentence qualifies the first. "Nonetheless" signals that. "Hence" implies the need for trials follows from the success, "Specifically" introduces detail, and "Similarly" signals likeness.

qs.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Kelp forests grow along rocky coasts in cool ocean waters.
  • Seagrass meadows grow in shallow, sandy areas in warm and temperate waters.
  • Both kelp forests and seagrass meadows absorb carbon dioxide as they grow.
  • Both provide shelter for many species of young fish.
qs.q: The student wants to emphasize similarities between kelp forests and seagrass meadows. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
c: Although they grow in different settings, kelp forests and seagrass meadows both absorb carbon dioxide and shelter many species of young fish.
Seagrass meadows absorb carbon dioxide as they grow.
Kelp forests grow along rocky coasts in cool ocean waters.
Kelp forests grow along rocky coasts, while seagrass meadows grow in shallow, sandy areas.
qs.e: Only choice A names both ecosystems and states what they share. Choice D states a difference, and choices B and C describe a single ecosystem.

qs.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • In a 2019 study, researchers turned in more than 17,000 "lost" wallets in 40 countries.
  • Some wallets contained no money; others contained a small amount of cash.
  • The researchers recorded how often each wallet's "owner" was contacted.
  • Wallets containing money were returned more often than wallets containing none.
  • Many people had predicted the opposite result.
qs.q: The student wants to emphasize the study's surprising result. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
c: Contrary to what many people predicted, a 2019 study in 40 countries found that lost wallets containing money were returned more often than wallets containing none.
In a 2019 study, researchers turned in more than 17,000 "lost" wallets in 40 countries.
Researchers recorded how often the "owners" of lost wallets were contacted.
Some of the wallets in the 2019 study contained a small amount of cash.
qs.e: Emphasizing a surprise requires the result and what it contradicted. Choice A gives both. The others describe the study's scale, method, or design without reporting the result.

qs.p:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • A mashrabiya is a projecting window enclosed by a carved wooden lattice.
  • Mashrabiyas are found in traditional architecture across the Middle East and North Africa.
  • The lattice blocks direct sunlight while still letting breezes pass through.
  • It also allows people inside to look out without being easily seen from the street.
qs.q: The student wants to explain the functions of a mashrabiya. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
c: Mashrabiyas are a feature of traditional architecture with wooden lattices.
A mashrabiya is a projecting window enclosed by a carved wooden lattice.
Mashrabiyas are found in traditional architecture across the Middle East and North Africa.
A mashrabiya's carved wooden lattice blocks direct sunlight while letting breezes through, and it lets people inside see out without being easily seen.
qs.e: Functions are what the feature does. Only choice D explains them: shade, ventilation, and privacy. The others describe where mashrabiyas are found or what they look like.

qs.q: If x5 + 3 = 7, what is the value of x?
qs.e: Subtract 3 from both sides: x/5 = 4. Multiply both sides by 5: x = 20.

qs.q: Which of the following points lies on the graph of 3x − 2y = 12 in the xy-plane?
A car rental costs $45 per day plus a one-time fee of $30. If the total cost of a rental is $345, for how many days was the car rented?
42 is 30% of what number?
qs.e: If 0.30n = 42, then n = 42 ÷ 0.30 = 140. (12.6 is 30% of 42, which answers a different question.)

qs.q: Which expression is equivalent to x2 + 5x − 24?
qs.e: Find two numbers with product −24 and sum 5: 8 and −3. So x2 + 5x − 24 = (x + 8)(x − 3). (x − 8)(x + 3) gives −5x, and the other pairs give sums of 2 and 10.

qs.q: The function f is defined by f(x) = 4x − 9. If f(2a) = 23, what is the value of a?
qs.e: f(2a) = 4(2a) − 9 = 8a − 9. Setting 8a − 9 = 23 gives 8a = 32 and a = 4. (Solving 4x − 9 = 23 gives x = 8, which is 2a, not a.)

qs.q: The mean of a list of 6 numbers is 15. If each number in the list is increased by 4, what is the mean of the new list?
qs.e: Adding 4 to each of the 6 numbers increases the total by 24 and the mean by 24 ÷ 6 = 4. The new mean is 19. (Adding 24 to the mean confuses the total increase with the increase per number.)

qs.q: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle (the angle between its two equal sides) of 36°. What is the measure of each base angle?
qs.e: The two base angles are equal and the three angles sum to 180°: 2b + 36 = 180, so b = 72°.

qs.q: Water flows into an empty tank at a rate of 12 liters per minute while draining out at a rate of 5 liters per minute. To the nearest tenth of a minute, how long will it take for the tank to contain 280 liters of water?
qs.e: The net rate is 12 − 5 = 7 liters per minute, so 280 liters takes 280 ÷ 7 = 40 minutes. Adding the rates gives 16.5, ignoring the drain gives 23.3, and using only the drain rate gives 56.

qs.q: The line graph shows a hardware store's sales for each of the first six months of a year. Between which two consecutive months did sales increase by the greatest amount?
qs.e: The month-to-month changes are: Jan–Feb +3, Feb–Mar −1, Mar–Apr +6, Apr–May +3, May–Jun −1 (thousand dollars). The largest increase, $6,000, was from March to April.

qs.q:
y = −2x + 10
y = x − 2
If (x, y) is the solution to the system of equations above, what is the value of y?
qs.e: Set the right sides equal: −2x + 10 = x − 2, so 12 = 3x and x = 4. Then y = 4 − 2 = 2.

qs.q: If 3a = 5, what is the value of 32a + 1?
qs.e: 32a + 1 = (3a)2 · 31 = 52 · 3 = 75. Adding exponents means multiplying powers, so 32a · 3 = 25 · 3, not 25 + 3 or 2 · 5 + 1.

qs.q: Which expression is equivalent to x2 − 4x2 − x − 2, for x > 2?
qs.e: Factor both: x2 − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2) and x2 − x − 2 = (x − 2)(x + 1). Cancel the common factor x − 2 to get (x + 2)/(x + 1).

qs.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 40 centimeters, and its length is 4 times its width. What is the area of the rectangle, in square centimeters?
qs.e: Let the width be w; the length is 4w. Perimeter: 2(w + 4w) = 10w = 40, so w = 4 and the length is 16. Area = 4 × 16 = 64.

qs.q: A sphere has a volume of 36π cubic inches. What is the radius of the sphere, in inches?
qs.e: Use V = (4/3)πr3: (4/3)πr3 = 36π, so r3 = 27 and r = 3.

qs.q: The value V, in dollars, of a phone t years after it is purchased is modeled by V = 800 − 150t. What is the best interpretation of 150 in this context?
c: The phone loses $150 in value each year.
The phone will be worth $150 after one year.
The phone loses 150% of its value each year.
qs.e: 150 is the coefficient of t, so it is the rate of change: the value decreases by $150 for each year. The purchase price is the value at t = 0, which is $800, and after one year the phone is worth $650.

The table summarizes a survey of 200 students. What fraction of the students who play an instrument are in grade 10?
qs.e: Restrict to students who play an instrument: 75. Of these, 45 are in grade 10, so the fraction is 45/75 = 3/5. (9/20 = 45/100 is the fraction of grade 10 students who play, which answers a different question.)

qs.q: In right triangle PQR, angle R is a right angle, cos P = 0.6, and PR = 9. What is the length of PQ?
qs.e: PR is adjacent to angle P, and PQ, opposite the right angle, is the hypotenuse. cos P = PR/PQ, so 0.6 = 9/PQ and PQ = 15. (5.4 multiplies instead of divides; 12 is the remaining leg, QR.)

qs.q: What is the positive solution to the equation 2x2 + 3x − 20 = 0?
qs.e: Factor: (2x − 5)(x + 4) = 0, so x = 5/2 or x = −4. The positive solution is 5/2 = 2.5. (Check: 2(6.25) + 7.5 − 20 = 0.)

qs.q: A circle in the xy-plane has its center at the origin and passes through the point (5, 12). Which of the following points also lies on the circle?
qs.e: The radius is √5² + 12² = 13, so a point is on the circle if its distance from the origin is 13. (−5, −12): √25 + 144 = 13 ✓. The others give √194, √109, and √145.

qs.q: How many integer values of x satisfy the inequality |2x + 1| ≤ 7?
qs.e: |2x + 1| ≤ 7 means −7 ≤ 2x + 1 ≤ 7, so −8 ≤ 2x ≤ 6 and −4 ≤ x ≤ 3. The integers are −4, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3: eight values. (Subtracting the endpoints, 3 − (−4) = 7, undercounts by one.)

qs.q: The function f is defined by f(x) = ax + b, where a and b are constants and a > 0. If f(f(x)) = 9x − 8 for all values of x, what is the value of b?
qs.e: f(f(x)) = a(ax + b) + b = a2x + ab + b. Matching coefficients: a2 = 9, so a = 3, and 3b + b = 4b = −8, so b = −2.

qs.q: If 3(2x − 1) − 2(x + 4) = 9, what is the value of x?
qs.e: Distribute: 6x − 3 − 2x − 8 = 9, so 4x − 11 = 9, 4x = 20, and x = 5. (20 is the value of 4x.)

qs.q: Which of the following equations has solutions x = −3 and x = 5?
qs.e: Solutions −3 and 5 mean factors (x + 3)(x − 5) = x2 − 2x − 15. The first choice factors as (x + 5)(x − 3), whose solutions have the wrong signs.

qs.q: The population of a species of fish in a lake t years after it was introduced is modeled by P(t) = 2,000(1.5)t/10. According to the model, after how many years will the population reach 4,500?
The temperature T, in degrees Fahrenheit, of a cup of tea t minutes after it is poured is modeled by T = 70 + 110(0.95)t. What is the best interpretation of the number 70 in this model?
c: The temperature of the tea when it is poured
The number of degrees the tea cools each minute
The percent by which the tea's temperature decreases each minute
The temperature the tea approaches as time passes, such as the room's temperature
qs.e: As t grows, (0.95)t approaches 0, so T approaches 70. That is the temperature the tea cools toward. The initial temperature is 70 + 110 = 180°F, and the model doesn't subtract a fixed number of degrees each minute.

qs.q: Which expression is equivalent to x3 − 8x − 2, for x ≠ 2?
qs.e: A difference of cubes factors as x3 − 8 = (x − 2)(x2 + 2x + 4). Check: x3 + 2x2 + 4x − 2x2 − 4x − 8 = x3 − 8. Dividing by x − 2 leaves x2 + 2x + 4.

qs.q: A square is inscribed in a circle with radius 5√2 centimeters. What is the area of the square, in square centimeters?
qs.e: The diagonal of an inscribed square is a diameter of the circle: 10√2. A square with diagonal 10√2 has side 10√2/√2 = 10, so its area is 100.

qs.q: The data set 3, 5, 5, 7, 10, k has a mean equal to its median. Which of the following is the value of k?
qs.e: The known values sum to 30. If k ≤ 5, the median is (5 + 5)/2 = 5, and a mean of 5 requires (30 + k)/6 = 5, so k = 0, which fits. Check the others: k = 6 gives median 5.5 and mean 6; k = 7.5 gives median 6 and mean 6.25; k = 12 gives median 6 and mean 7.

qs.q: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon measures 24°. How many sides does the polygon have?
qs.e: The exterior angles of any polygon sum to 360°. With equal exterior angles of 24°, the number of sides is 360 ÷ 24 = 15.

qs.q: If x1/2 = 3y, where x > 0 and y > 0, which of the following is equal to x3/2?
qs.e: x3/2 = (x1/2)3 = (3y)3 = 27y3. Cubing only the y (to get 3y3) forgets to cube the 3.

qs.q: The numbers a and b satisfy 1a + 1b = 56 and ab = 6. What is the value of a + b?
qs.e: Combine the fractions: 1/a + 1/b = (b + a)/(ab). So (a + b)/6 = 5/6, giving a + b = 5. (The numbers are 2 and 3.)

qs.q: In a 30°-60°-90° triangle, the side opposite the 60° angle has length 9. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
qs.e: The sides are in the ratio s : s√3 : 2s. The side opposite 60° is s√3 = 9, so s = 9/√3 = 3√3, and the hypotenuse is 2s = 6√3. (18 assumes the 9 is the short leg.)

qs.q: A rectangular garden is bordered on one side by a wall. The other three sides are enclosed by 60 meters of fencing. What is the maximum possible area of the garden, in square meters?
qs.e: Let x be the length of each side perpendicular to the wall; the side parallel to the wall is 60 − 2x. Area = x(60 − 2x) = −2x2 + 60x, which is greatest at x = 15. Maximum area: 15 × 30 = 450. (225 assumes a 15-by-15 square, which would need fencing on all four sides.)

qs.q:
Score1234
Frequency2k53
The table shows the frequency of each score in a data set. If the mean of the data set is 2.6, what is the value of k?
In the xy-plane, the line passing through the points (1, 2) and (4, 11) intersects the line y = −x + 10 at the point (a, b). What is the value of a?
qs.e: The first line has slope (11 − 2)/(4 − 1) = 3, so y = 3x − 1. Setting 3x − 1 = −x + 10 gives 4x = 11 and x = 11/4 = 2.75.

qs.q: The endpoints of a diameter of a circle in the xy-plane are (−2, 3) and (6, −3). Which of the following is an equation of the circle?
qs.e: The center is the midpoint: ((−2 + 6)/2, (3 + (−3))/2) = (2, 0). The diameter's length is √8² + 6² = 10, so the radius is 5 and r2 = 25. The equation is (x − 2)2 + y2 = 25. Using 100 squares the diameter instead of the radius.

qs.q: Six workers, all working at the same rate, can paint a building in 10 days. At the same rate, how many days would it take 4 workers to paint the building?
qs.e: The job requires 6 × 10 = 60 worker-days. With 4 workers: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 days. Fewer workers take longer, so the answer must exceed 10; 6.7 treats the relationship as direct rather than inverse.

qs.q: The function f is defined by f(x) = x2 − 8x + 20. For what value of k does the equation f(x) = k have exactly one solution?
qs.e: A horizontal line y = k meets an upward-opening parabola exactly once only at the vertex. The vertex is at x = 4, where f(4) = 16 − 32 + 20 = 4. So k = 4.

qs.q: The graph of a quadratic function in the xy-plane has x-intercepts at x = 2 and x = −3 and a y-intercept at y = −6. Which equation defines the function?
qs.e: The function has the form y = a(x − 2)(x + 3). At x = 0: a(−2)(3) = −6a = −6, so a = 1, and y = x2 + x − 6. The last choice has the right intercepts but a y-intercept of −12; the third has a y-intercept of 6.

qs.q: For an acute angle θ, tan θ = 724. What is the value of cos θ − sin θ?
qs.e: With opposite 7 and adjacent 24, the hypotenuse is √7² + 24² = 25. So cos θ = 24/25 and sin θ = 7/25, and cos θ − sin θ = 17/25. (31/25 is their sum.)

qs.q: A solid consists of a right circular cylinder with radius 3 inches and height 10 inches, topped by a hemisphere with the same radius. The volume of the solid is kπ cubic inches. What is the value of k?
qs.e: Cylinder: π(3)2(10) = 90π. Hemisphere: half of (4/3)π(3)3 = (1/2)(36π) = 18π. Total: 108π, so k = 108.

qs.q: The first term of a sequence is 3, and each term after the first is −2 times the preceding term. What is the sixth term of the sequence?
qs.e: The nth term is 3(−2)n − 1. The sixth term is 3(−2)5 = 3(−32) = −96. The terms alternate in sign: 3, −6, 12, −24, 48, −96.

qs.q: A rhombus has sides of length 13, and one of its diagonals has length 24. What is the area of the rhombus?
qs.e: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, forming four right triangles with hypotenuse 13 and one leg 24/2 = 12. The other leg is √13² − 12² = 5, so the other diagonal is 10. Area = (1/2)(24)(10) = 120.
